rationale: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-02, verbatim in substance: 'please fix both'. Two FCA rule citations in lendzy's live copy are wrong (verified against the handbook text, every quote checked on 2026-09-02): the two-rollover limit is attributed to CONC 6.7.17, which is the DEFINITIONS rule — the limit is CONC 6.7.23 ('A firm must not refinance high-cost short-term credit (other than by exercising forbearance) on more than two occasions'); and the two-attempt continuous-payment-authority limit is attributed to CONC 6.7.23 — the refinance rule — when it is CONC 7.6.12. Both substantive claims are true; only the rule numbers move. A fleet census of all five storage surfaces (content_data, page rendered_html, site_components, current specs, component templates) found every occurrence: lendzy's 13 content rows, its content_direction SPEC (the writing instructions carry the CPA error twice — the source that would RE-PLANT it on any rewrite, the bugs_closed/414 lesson), its rollover tool template, and ONE propagation: loancash.co.uk serves the same wrong rollover cite via a fork of lendzy's tool (component 6525121a), measured live at its /tools/rollover-limit-checker/ page. Included because it is our sentence propagated by our fork mechanism. The fix is two verbatim token substitutions, NOT an LLM rewrite — an LLM rewrite risks prose drift the owner did not authorise, and the tool templates carry ~51 live '{{' bindings a rewrite could disturb where a token replace cannot.

plan.summary: One migration (696), no Go. Seven DO/RAISE guards pin the exact censused pre-state (counts AND row counts per surface, plus completeness guards asserting NOTHING else fleet-wide carries either token). Then ordered token replaces — CPA first (CONC 6.7.23 -> CONC 7.6.12) while every stored 6.7.23 is the CPA error, rollover second (CONC 6.7.17 -> CONC 6.7.23) minting the legitimate 6.7.23s; reversed, the rollover fix would be destroyed by the CPA replace. The content_direction spec is SUPERSEDED via a single CTE (UPDATE ... RETURNING feeding the INSERT, so an older superseded row cannot be resurrected), history kept. rendered_html is corrected in the same pass so a bugs-260-class carry ships corrected bytes. Eleven page_rerender items are filed in the same transaction (the 693 round-2 lesson: a repair that queues nothing satisfies none of its own acceptance criteria). DO/RAISE verify: CONC 6.7.17 extinct on every surface, exact post-counts, the corrected spec is the single current row, 11 rerenders queued.
plan.risks: (1) A blanket reverse cannot roll this back: the tool-cpa-cancellation-checker template and page carried a CORRECT 'CONC 7.6.12' BEFORE 696, so the ROLLBACK is enumerated by page name and ordered (6.7.23->6.7.17 first, then 7.6.12->6.7.23 scoped to the changed rows only), with a verify arm asserting the cpa tool's pre-existing correct citation SURVIVED the reverse. (2) Race with content writes between census and apply: guards pin counts AND row counts on every surface and abort on any drift, including G7 completeness guards for rows born elsewhere. (3) Stacking rerenders: guarded — aborts if any live item carries one of the 11 keys. (4) The rerenders regenerate section HTML from corrected content_data; for the two tool pages the template renders through ~51 live bindings — a token replace inside a text literal cannot alter a binding, and the acceptance check is at the ARTEFACT: both tool URLs must serve 'CONC 6.7.23' (rollover) with unchanged input counts, and the seven content pages must serve 'CONC 7.6.12' in CPA context and nothing must serve 'CONC 6.7.17' anywhere. (5) Cross-site scope: one loancash component + one loancash rerender. Stated to the owner, who also ruled today that the other finance sites do their register work — this migration fixes only the propagated verbatim error, nothing else on loancash. (6) A chassis roll is expected within the hour: the migration is DB config and unaffected, but it will be APPLIED after the roll settles (no dispatch within ~300s of a chassis restart), so the rerender pickup does not race the restart.
